objectives.title: Interpretability
objectives.text: Understand how the acquisition of transcriptomics data constrains the way we analyse those data and the way we interpret the results.

objectives.title: Systems thinking
objectives.text: Think in systems: connect concepts as graphs, with the mind map and the Biolink activity.

objectives.title: Reproducibility
objectives.text: Produce analyses that another person can rerun and obtain the same numbers, through the practical sessions.

objectives.title: Provenance, transparency and collaborative translational science
objectives.text: Record where data and results come from, work in the open, and collaborate with shared tooling such as GitHub.

courses.title: Biological Hierarchy, the Central Dogma, and the Nucleus
courses.summary: Start with the biological hierarchy, the central dogma, and the idea that every transcriptomic measurement begins as a molecule in a cell.

video.label: Course 1, Central Dogma and the Nucleus (20:09), SandrineTeach channel

references.text: Lander E., 7.012 Introduction to Biology (Fall 2004) and 7.016 Introductory Biology (Fall 2018), MIT OpenCourseWare. The lecture videos on transcription and translation treat the content of this course in more depth
MITx 7.00x, Introduction to Biology, The Secret of Life (E. Lander), self-paced
Crick F. Central dogma of molecular biology. Nature 227:561–563 (1970)
Schwanhäusser B. et al. Global quantification of mammalian gene expression control. Nature 473:337–342 (2011). Source for the half-lives of messenger RNA and proteins
Liu Y., Beyer A., Aebersold R. On the dependency of cellular protein levels on mRNA abundance. Cell 165:535–550 (2016). Source for the relation between RNA and protein levels
Alberts B. et al. Molecular Biology of the Cell, chapters 6–7
yourgenome (Wellcome Sanger Institute), animation From DNA to protein: 3D, shown in section 4

Luecken M.D., Theis F.J. Current best practices in single-cell RNA-seq analysis: a tutorial. Molecular Systems Biology 15:e8746 (2019). The best practical starting point for quality control in single-cell data
